Bedrock raises $600M to expand autonomous excavators on construction sites

CapitalG and Emergence lead the Series C as Bedrock expands field support and contractor deployments after beginning paid autonomous work.

GlobeNewswire ↗26 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Capital for deployment capacity

Bedrock Robotics announced a $600 million Series C at a $4.1 billion post-money valuation, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital. Total financing is now nearly $1 billion. The company plans to expand deployed equipment and contractor support, including the field organization needed beyond research.

Retrofitting existing equipment

Bedrock develops autonomy retrofits for heavy equipment, starting with excavators. It says fully autonomous paid work on live sites began in mid-August 2026. New partner Haydon is deploying the technology in Texas, while additional customers extend its footprint into states including Minnesota and Florida.

Further applications remain trials

Haydon plans to test trench work and larger machine models; the announcement does not establish autonomous readiness for every proposed task. Funding also supports field, commercial and operating teams. Independently verified hourly costs, accident rates and productivity comparisons with human operation are not supplied.
